paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers met at the railway station. Teacher Kim counted the members of the club, and everyone was there. Leo had a small book in his bag for his cartoons. Lily held the tickets for her group. The station was busy, and many people stood on the platform with bags. Then the speaker on the wall made a loud sound. The children stopped and listened.

"Listen, please. Today is Saturday, the third of October. The train to the coast leaves from platform two at ten past nine. The journey takes one hour. The train arrives at ten past ten. Please stand behind the yellow line. Do not run on the platform. Do not leave your bag alone.
"The train back to town leaves the coast at midday. Another train leaves at half past twelve. Please keep your ticket with you all day. Thank you."

"What time does our train leave?" asked Mia. "At ten past nine," said Lily. "Look at the big clock." "Where is platform two?" asked Leo. "It is over the bridge," said Lily. The children walked over the bridge and found the right platform. It was five past nine, so the children had time. "Perhaps we can sit next to the window," said Mia. "Perhaps we can see the sea from the train."

On the train, Leo drew a cartoon of the speaker. In the cartoon, the speaker had a very big mouth. It said, "Please stand behind the yellow line!" The members laughed when they saw it. Leo showed it to Teacher Kim, and she smiled. At ten past ten, the train arrived at the coast. "Remember," said Teacher Kim, "our train home leaves at midday." "We have two hours here." The sea was blue and calm. A cool wind came from the sea, and the children put on their hats.
